scenes.tts: If C-tactile input makes a stroke feel pleasant, what happens when that input is taken away?
scenes.visual: Title card: Take the Input Away. A brush on a forearm, with the CT fibre fading out. Question on screen: what happens to pleasantness?
scenes.narration: If C-tactile input makes a stroke feel pleasant, what happens when that input is taken away?

scenes.tts: No one can remove a fibre class from a healthy person. But some people have lost part of their touch pathway.
scenes.visual: Three silhouettes, each with a different part of the touch pathway greyed out.
scenes.narration: No one can remove a fibre class from a healthy person. But some people have lost part of their touch pathway.

scenes.tts: Start with the reverse case. In two thousand two, Olausson and colleagues studied a patient lacking large myelinated afferents.
scenes.caption: Start with the reverse case. In 2002, Olausson and colleagues studied a patient lacking large myelinated afferents.
scenes.visual: The first silhouette: thick myelinated fibres greyed out, thin C fibres intact. Label: Olausson and colleagues, 2002; one patient.
scenes.narration: Start with the reverse case. In 2002, Olausson and colleagues studied a patient lacking large myelinated afferents.

scenes.tts: Stroking that excites C-tactile afferents produced a faint, pleasant sensation.
scenes.visual: A brush strokes hairy skin. A faint label appears: pleasant, faint.
scenes.narration: Stroking that excites C-tactile afferents produced a faint, pleasant sensation.

scenes.tts: Imaging showed insular activation, and none detectable in primary or secondary somatosensory cortex.
scenes.visual: A brain schematic: the insular region lit; primary and secondary somatosensory cortex dark. Caption: functional MRI, one patient.
scenes.narration: Imaging showed insular activation, and none detectable in primary or secondary somatosensory cortex.

scenes.tts: One patient shows what this input can do without large fibres, not that it is needed.
scenes.visual: Label: CT input without large myelinated fibres can do this. Below it, struck through: needed.
scenes.narration: One patient shows what this input can do without large fibres, not that it is needed.

scenes.tts: Next, ten carriers of a nerve growth factor mutation. They have fewer thin and unmyelinated fibres.
scenes.caption: Next, ten carriers of a nerve growth factor mutation (HSAN type V). They have fewer thin and unmyelinated fibres.
scenes.visual: The second silhouette: the C-fibre density icon thins. Label: HSAN type V, nerve growth factor beta mutation; Morrison and colleagues, 2011.
scenes.narration: Next, ten carriers of a nerve growth factor mutation (HSAN type V). They have fewer thin and unmyelinated fibres.

scenes.tts: Predict. How should they rate slow stroking at the speeds C-tactile afferents prefer?
scenes.visual: Two empty rating bars, carriers and matched controls, at the CT-optimal speed. Text: predict.
scenes.narration: Predict. How should they rate slow stroking at the speeds C-tactile afferents prefer?

scenes.tts: They rated it less pleasant than matched controls. And their posterior insula was not modulated by that stroking.
scenes.visual: The carriers' bar fills lower than the controls'. A small insula icon stays flat for the carriers.
scenes.narration: They rated it less pleasant than matched controls. And their posterior insula was not modulated by that stroking.

scenes.tts: The mutation affects more than C-tactile afferents, so this is not a clean removal.
scenes.visual: Label: affects more fibres than CT afferents alone.
scenes.narration: The mutation affects more than C-tactile afferents, so this is not a clean removal.

scenes.tts: Now cut a route instead. An anterolateral cordotomy cuts part of the spinal cord to relieve intractable pain.
scenes.visual: A spinal cord cross-section; the anterolateral quadrant is cut. Label: anterolateral cordotomy.
scenes.narration: Now cut a route instead. An anterolateral cordotomy cuts part of the spinal cord to relieve intractable pain.

scenes.tts: In two thousand nineteen, Marshall and colleagues tested such patients before and after, with a brush at three speeds.
scenes.caption: In 2019, Marshall and colleagues tested such patients before and after, with a brush at three speeds.
scenes.visual: Label: Marshall and colleagues, 2019; 19 adults with refractory cancer pain, tested before and after.
scenes.narration: In 2019, Marshall and colleagues tested such patients before and after, with a brush at three speeds.

scenes.tts: Predict. Pain and temperature travel in that tract. If pleasant touch travelled only there, what should the cut do?
scenes.visual: Pain, temperature and itch icons sit on the cut quadrant. Prediction card: ratings vanish?
scenes.narration: Predict. Pain and temperature travel in that tract. If pleasant touch travelled only there, what should the cut do?

scenes.tts: Pain, temperature and itch were markedly disrupted. But pleasantness ratings were not significantly changed.
scenes.visual: Pain, temperature and itch icons fade. Three rating bars, before and after, stay essentially the same height.
scenes.narration: Pain, temperature and itch were markedly disrupted. But pleasantness ratings were not significantly changed.

scenes.tts: With nineteen patients, that is not proof of no change. But the ratings did not vanish.
scenes.caption: With 19 patients, that is not proof of no change. But the ratings did not vanish.
scenes.visual: Label: not significantly changed is not the same as unchanged.
scenes.narration: With 19 patients, that is not proof of no change. But the ratings did not vanish.

scenes.tts: The authors proposed a route outside that tract, most likely the dorsal columns.
scenes.visual: The dorsal columns highlight on the cross-section. Label: proposed route.
scenes.narration: The authors proposed a route outside that tract, most likely the dorsal columns.

scenes.tts: So the two tests ask different questions. With fewer thin fibres, carriers rated caress-speed stroking as less pleasant.
scenes.visual: Split screen, left: reduced thin-fibre density, rating bar lower. Label: input reduced, not only CT fibres.
scenes.narration: So the two tests ask different questions. With fewer thin fibres, carriers rated caress-speed stroking as less pleasant.

scenes.tts: Cordotomy cut one route, yet pleasantness survived. Neither test shows which fibres carry the surviving signal.
scenes.visual: Split screen, right: route cut, rating bar unchanged. Label: surviving judgement, source unresolved. Caption across both: input versus route.
scenes.narration: Cordotomy cut one route, yet pleasantness survived. Neither test shows which fibres carry the surviving signal.

scenes.tts: So thin-fibre input seems to contribute, and this route is not needed. C-tactile input remains a candidate, its route unresolved.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: input reduced, pleasantness falls; route cut, pleasantness survives; CT input remains a candidate, route unresolved.
scenes.narration: So thin-fibre input seems to contribute, and this route is not needed. C-tactile input remains a candidate, its route unresolved.
